claims.planned: Confirm the site is live (Sept 2026), its current URL/ownership (it was reported to have moved under LabEx), and the names of its lesson tracks so pages can point at matching lessons
claims.finding: Live. linuxjourney.com now 301-redirects to https://labex.io/linuxjourney — link to the LabEx URL. Ownership: maintained by LabEx; GitHub repo labex-labs/linuxjourney ('The official Linux Journey (formerly linuxjourney.com) source repository is maintained by LabEx', ~1.5k stars, last push 2026-09-02); the original cindyq/linuxjourney repo path redirects there (repo transferred). Tracks as listed on the page — GRASSHOPPER: Getting Started, Command Line, Text-Fu, Advanced Text-Fu, User Management, Permissions, Processes, Packages. JOURNEYMAN: Devices, The Filesystem, Boot the System, Kernel, Init, Process Utilization, Logging. NETWORKING NOMAD: Network Sharing, Network Basics, Subnetting, Routing, Network Config, Troubleshooting, DNS. All planned track names are present. Course URL pattern reported: /linuxjourney/courses/<course-name> (e.g. /linuxjourney/courses/getting-started) — not independently verified because raw HTML was blocked; link to the landing page rather than deep links unless an author checks them in a browser. Caveat: page text was obtained through WebFetch's summarising model (bot challenge blocked curl), so treat the quotes as near-verbatim.
claims.quote: Linux Journey is maintained by LabEx as a free, open-source, community-driven Linux learning project.
claims.location: labex.io/linuxjourney landing page (as rendered by WebFetch); HTTP headers of linuxjourney.com; GitHub repo description

extra_findings: Attribution line on the page: 'Linux Journey was originally created by Cindy Quach in 2015 to help beginners learn Linux.' (via WebFetch rendering)

Free/no sign-up: 'No cost, no sign-up required. Open to everyone, forever.' and 'Linux Journey remains free to use, just as it has since its creation.' LabEx adds: 'LabEx continues to preserve the original learning philosophy while expanding the platform with practical Linux labs and exercises.' (LabEx's own labs are a commercial product; the Linux Journey lessons themselves are stated to be free.)

Suggested mapping for 'further practice' pointers: shell pages -> Command Line; text processing -> Text-Fu / Advanced Text-Fu; users & permissions -> User Management, Permissions; processes/signals -> Processes; resources -> Process Utilization; logs -> Logging; mounts/FHS -> The Filesystem, Devices; packages -> Packages; systemd -> Init; networking -> Network Basics, Subnetting, Routing, DNS, Troubleshooting. (Mapping is the verifier's suggestion from track names only; lesson contents were not reviewed.)
teaching_notes: Pointer only, as planned. Use https://labex.io/linuxjourney (the old domain redirects). Site is behind a Cloudflare bot challenge, so automated link checkers will report 403 — that is not a dead link. Do not cite it as evidence for any technical fact.
